To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electric field-induced rearrangement of magnetic domain boundaries in magnetic dielectrics with easy magnetization anisotropy is due to the magnetoelectric effect.

1. the electric field-induced displacement of the magnetic DB occurs due to the electrostatic interaction between the electric field and the magnetic DB, 2. the displacement distance of the magnetic DB is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the DB and the electric field source, and 3. the electric field magnitude required for DB displacement is inversely proportional the distance between the magnetic DB and the electric charge source.
the electric field can be used to control the position of magnetic domain walls, which is important for applications of magnetic films in magnetic recording, spintronics, etc.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the magnetoelectric properties of magnetic DBs and the effect of an electric field on the displacement and transformation of DBs.
the magnetoelectric interactions in the magnetic dielectric materials, which are of interest in the development of magnetoelectronic devices.

the mechanisms of the electric field-induced displacement and transformation of magnetic DB in thin films of a magnetic dielectrics with uniaxial anisotropy and the formation of a magnetic domain structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electric field can induce a displacement of the magnetic domain boundaries and a change in their shape and orientation.

the electric field can induce a transformation of the magnetic DB, i.e. the electric field can cause the DB to be displaced from the source location and the DB can be transformed into an electric field source, i.e. an electric dipole, which is oriented in the direction of the electric field vector.

the electric field-induced displacement and transformation of a magnetic DB in a film of magnetic dielectric is a consequence of the electro-magnetic interaction between the electric field and the DB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electro-induced displacement and rearrangement of magnetic DB in a film of magnetic dielectric with anisotropy of the easy magnetization axis is possible.
the electric field can be used to displace the DB and transform the micromagnetic state of the sample.
a magnetic domain boundary is a source of electric charge, the magnitude of which increases as the electric field magnitude increases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electric field can induce a displacement of magnetic DB and the formation of a magnetic domain structure in a magnetic dielectric film with easy magnetization anisotropy.
the electric field can be used as an effective means to induce a transformation in magnetic DBs.
